description:
On Cassini, every flyby event in the /fly CAPCOM event ticker reads 'FLYBY' with an empty note, instead of showing the event's proper name and description (e.g. 'Venus #1 — gravity assist' with a description of the 284 km closest approach). The milestone chips on the canvas render the correct labels.

Expected: For mission events whose base `flight.events[]` carry a `label` and `description`, those values should appear in the CAPCOM event ticker as the event label and note, respectively. Only events without a `label` should fall back to the generic type label (e.g. 'FLYBY').

Acceptance criteria:
- Cassini flyby at MET 617 shows label 'Venus #2 — gravity assist' and a non-empty note in the CAPCOM ticker, not 'FLYBY' with empty note [reporter: 'On Cassini every flyby in the event ticker just says \'FLYBY\' with an empty note. The mission data definitely has proper names for these events.']
- Cassini flyby at MET 672 shows label 'Earth — gravity assist' and a non-empty note in the CAPCOM ticker [reporter: Same report — 'every flyby' includes the Earth gravity assist]
- Cassini flyby at MET 1172 shows label 'Jupiter — gravity assist' and a non-empty note in the CAPCOM ticker [reporter: Same report — 'every flyby' includes the Jupiter gravity assist]
- Structural events that lack a `label` field still fall back to the default type-based label (e.g. 'FLYBY') with empty note [code-invariant: mergeFlightEvents() DEFAULT_FLIGHT_LABELS must remain the fallback for label-less structural events]
- Editorial overlay events still take precedence over structural events at MET collisions (within 0.05 day tolerance) [code-invariant: mergeFlightEvents() editorial-precedence rule must be preserved]
